name: AIGRCeler regulatory map
note: How AIGRCeler covers ISO/IEC 42001:2023, the EU AI Act and the NIST AI RMF 1.0. Indicative pointers for traceability, not legal advice and not a statement that the company complies. Whether a duty applies is a question for counsel.

mechanisms.workspace: Company workspace: people, roles, authority basis, risk-acceptance thresholds, principles, company-level risks
mechanisms.stages: Four stages (Discover, Assess, Govern, Operate); each starts by a named person's decision, the first three close at a gate, and the go decision in Operate is a named person's decision
mechanisms.lanes: Three lanes scale the effort to the risk
mechanisms.journal: Decision journal: hash-chained, decisions in the decision-maker's own words
mechanisms.risk: Risk method: standard scenarios, inherent and residual ratings, credit only from verified controls, acceptance by threshold
mechanisms.catalog: Control catalog owned by AI Governance: versions, proposals, release
mechanisms.evidence: Evidence intake, analysis, strength and expiry
mechanisms.indicators: Indicators with tolerances; credit suspended when out of tolerance
mechanisms.incidents: Incident handling with response clocks, obligations and retrospectives
mechanisms.review: Review stage: periodic and after-incident review, catalog improvement
mechanisms.profile: Discovery profile: structured facts about the system, who said them and when
mechanisms.requests: Requests to named people, one message per person, tracked until answered
mechanisms.views: Generated views: accountability matrix, trust-property view, risk view, waiting view, regulatory view
mechanisms.launch: Launch-status feed to the company's own pipeline
mechanisms.containment: Containment actions and stage blocks for ongoing harm or a possible legal hard stop

items.title: Understanding the organization and its context
items.note: External and internal issues are kept as company-level risks, per-system context notes and the charter's context section.

items.title: Needs and expectations of interested parties
items.note: Interested parties are named in the charter and per system in the impact assessment; affected people are consulted under GO-15.

items.title: Scope of the AI management system
items.note: Scope is the list of registered AI systems plus the charter's scope statement.

items.title: AI management system
items.note: AIGRCeler supplies the working management system (roles, stages, controls, records, review). Certification is a decision of an accredited body after audit of how the company operates it.

items.title: Leadership and commitment
items.note: Executive leadership accepts the highest residual risks and approves the principles; their acceptance is in the journal.

items.title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
items.note: Roles carry named people, a start date and the basis of their authority; every decision names who made it and on what basis.

items.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities (general)
AI risk assessment
items.note: Standard scenarios, rated before controls, scored in six dimensions, re-scored when facts or evidence change.

items.title: AI risk treatment
items.note: Controls are drafted from the risk, approved by AI Governance, and earn risk credit only when verified. Residual risk is accepted by a person with the right authority.

items.title: AI system impact assessment
items.note: GO-17 is the impact assessment on individuals, groups and society; GO-11 adds fundamental rights where they are at stake; HR-09 covers safety.

items.title: AI objectives and planning to achieve them
items.note: Objectives sit in the principles statement and the charter; indicators and the annual review measure them.

items.title: Planning of changes
items.note: Changes to a system need re-approval when they matter (GO-14); changes to the catalog go through proposals and a release decision.

items.title: Resources
items.note: Roles and people are named; AI expertise and readiness are tracked as company-level risks.

items.title: Communication
items.note: Messages to people are written in plain words, one per person, and tracked until answered.

items.title: Documented information
items.note: Records are written by the engine, chained, and kept for the period the lane requires.

items.title: AI risk assessment (operation)
items.note: Ratings are recomputed when evidence expires, a model version changes or an indicator leaves tolerance.

items.title: AI system impact assessment (operation)
items.note: The impact assessment is repeated at review and when the use changes.

items.title: Alignment with other organizational policies
items.note: GO-02 now requires the statement to say how it relates to security, privacy and ethics policies.

items.title: Review of the AI policy
items.note: GO-02 now requires a review date.

items.title: Reporting of concerns
items.note: GO-05 now requires staff to know how to raise a concern.

items.title: Tooling resources
items.note: Tools are suggested in playbooks and their use is recorded as evidence. AIGRCeler does not inventory the company's tools itself.

items.title: System and computing resources
items.note: Recovery and dependencies are covered; capacity planning is the company's own engineering practice and is only recorded, not checked.

items.title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups
Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
Objectives for responsible development of AI system
Processes for responsible design and development
Documentation of AI system design and development
AI system recording of event logs
Data for development and enhancement of AI system
Quality of data for AI systems
Data preparation
items.note: DG-06 now includes cleaning and labelling steps.

items.title: System documentation and information for users
Processes for responsible use of AI systems
Objectives for responsible use of AI system
Intended use of the AI system
Customers
items.note: Information for customers who receive the company's AI output is covered; responsibilities written into customer contracts are the company's legal work and are recorded only as evidence.

items.title: Prohibited AI practices
items.note: A possible prohibited use is raised at once, placed as a stage block, and put to counsel. AIGRCeler never states in its own voice that a use is lawful.

items.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
items.note: Records the company's classification and the reasoning; counsel decides.

items.title: Compliance with the requirements for high-risk systems
Transparency and provision of information to deployers
Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
Quality management system
items.note: Covers accountability, risk management, data management, testing, record-keeping, change control and post-market monitoring. Not covered by the starter catalog: the list of harmonised standards applied, and written communication procedures with national authorities beyond incident and regulator readiness. Counsel decides what the company's QMS document must contain.

items.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
Authorised representatives of providers
items.note: Applies when the provider is outside the EU; GO-18 asks whether a representative is needed and appointed.

items.title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
items.note: Includes informing workers or their representatives before a workplace deployment (GO-15) and human oversight by trained people (HR-01, HR-02).

items.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for deployers of high-risk AI systems
items.note: Applies to public bodies and some private deployers; counsel confirms who must do it.

items.title: Conformity assessment
items.note: AIGRCeler tracks the steps and keeps the records; the assessment itself (internal control or a notified body) is performed outside it.

items.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
General-purpose AI models
items.note: Covers the company as a user of a general-purpose model: it obtains the provider's documentation (TP-14). The duties of the provider of such a model are out of the starter catalog's scope; a company that itself places a general-purpose model on the market needs its own legal plan.

items.title: Reporting of serious incidents
items.note: Regulator notice periods are tracked as obligations with their own clocks.

items.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
Legal and regulatory requirements are understood, managed and documented
Trustworthy AI characteristics are integrated into policies and processes
items.note: Every control carries trust-property tags; view 4 shows them.

items.title: Processes set the level of risk management by the organization's risk tolerance
The risk management process is set through transparent policies and procedures
Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process
Processes decommission and phase out AI systems safely
Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication are documented
Personnel receive AI risk management training
Executive leadership takes responsibility for AI risk decisions
items.note: Executive leadership accepts the highest residual risks.

items.title: Decision-making involves a diverse team
items.note: Roles bring several functions to each system, and affected people are heard (GO-15). The make-up of the company's teams is the company's own matter and is not measured.

items.title: Policies define roles for human-AI configurations and oversight
Policies foster critical thinking and a safety-first mindset
items.note: Principles, training and screen design support it; culture itself is not something a control can prove.

items.title: Teams document and communicate risks and impacts
Practices support testing, incident identification and information sharing
Policies collect and consider input from external parties
Mechanisms incorporate feedback into design and use
Policies address third-party risks, including intellectual property
Intended purposes, context and applicable laws are understood
Interdisciplinary actors are involved
items.note: Questions go to business, engineering, security, legal and operations roles; one message per person.

items.title: The organization's mission and goals for AI are understood
Organizational risk tolerances are determined
items.note: Thresholds say who may accept which residual level.

items.title: System requirements are elicited from stakeholders
The tasks and methods the system supports are defined
Knowledge limits and how people oversee the output are documented
Scientific integrity and test, evaluation, verification and validation (TEVV) considerations are identified
Potential costs and negative impacts are examined
The targeted application scope is specified
Operator and practitioner proficiency is defined and assessed
Legal risks of components, including third-party, are mapped
Internal risk controls for third-party components exist
Likelihood and magnitude of each impact are identified
Practices engage relevant actors on impacts and collect feedback
Measurement approaches and metrics are selected, and unmeasured risks are documented
items.note: Known limits and facts nobody could supply are carried to Assess as concerns.

items.title: The appropriateness of metrics is regularly assessed and updated
Experts who did not build the system take part in assessments
items.note: Independent assessment is recommended in red-teaming and the yearly audit, and recorded, but not enforced; AIGRCeler agents are not independent of each other.

items.title: Test sets, metrics and TEVV details are documented
Evaluations involving people meet human-subject protection standards
items.note: Covered only for usability and accessibility testing with people; formal human-subject protection review is the company's own process.

items.title: Performance is demonstrated under conditions like deployment
The system is monitored in production
Transparency and accountability risks are examined
The model is explained and its output interpreted
Environmental impact and sustainability are assessed
items.note: Considered in the impact assessment; energy and emissions are not measured by AIGRCeler.

items.title: The effectiveness of the evaluation metrics is assessed
Approaches identify emergent risks over time
Risk is tracked where it is hard to assess
items.note: Facts that could not be learned are recorded as unknown, carried to Assess as concerns, and make the starting risk rating more cautious.

items.title: Feedback processes let end users report problems
Measurement approaches are connected to the deployment context
Measurement results are informed by domain experts
items.note: Owners and reviewers supply domain knowledge; there is no check that a domain expert reviewed each result.

items.title: Performance improvements and declines are documented
It is determined whether the system achieves its purpose and should proceed
Treatment of documented risks is prioritized
Responses to high-priority risks are developed and documented
Resources to manage risks are considered, including non-AI alternatives
Mechanisms sustain the value of deployed systems
Procedures respond to risks not known in advance
Mechanisms supersede, disengage or deactivate systems that perform inconsistently
Continual improvement is built into the process
Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant parties
